# Design: how memories attach to trails (COR-2110)

Version 3, approved 2026-10-14. Owner: evis. Implementation tickets: COR-2123 to COR-2127. Versions 1 and 2 are summarized at the end.

## Summary

A fact records which session, checkpoint, and commit produced it. These provenance anchors are written at creation and never change. Every consumer — the trail page, the repo Memories page, and a teammate's local brain — selects facts by querying these anchors. The branch name is not a key anywhere. Sync is per-fact: the client upserts facts up, and pulls a repo-wide delta down, filtered locally by git reachability from its own HEAD. Upload runs on the checkpoint event (per commit), on session end, and on the daemon tick.

## Problem

Memories are keyed by branch name at every layer:

- Local store: `facts/<slug>-<sha256(branch)[:4]>/facts.ndjson` (`internal/cli/facts.go`).
- Sync protocol: `GET/POST /api/v1/repos/{repoID}/brain/facts?branch=<name>` (`internal/factsync/httpserver.go`), one CAS set-head per `(repo, branch)`.
- Brainstore: `branch` is in the primary key of `brain_fact_heads`, `brain_facts`, and `brain_fact_events`. `/memories` filters `WHERE repo_id = $1 AND branch = $2`.

Branch names change. Three failure modes, all reported:

1. Rename (Conductor renames placeholder branches automatically): local facts stay in the old directory; the hosted head stays under the old name; the new name starts empty.
2. Delete after merge: the rows still exist under the old name, but no caller holds that name, so the trail UI gets an empty list.
3. Recycle: a new branch that reuses a deleted name syncs against the old head. The first pull imports the old facts into the new local store, and new facts publish into the old head.

A fourth problem surfaced during this design: with per-branch heads and no promote step, facts synced under a feature branch never enter the `main` head, so a teammate on main never receives them locally after the trail merges. Version 1 papered over this with a promote-on-merge event. Version 3 fixes it structurally.

## Facts about the current system that the design uses

- Fact identity is `sha256(normalized text + sorted paths)`. Branch is not part of the identity (`factmerge/record.go`).
- Fact status moves one way: active → superseded/retracted. Never back.
- Distill stamps each fact with provenance anchors: SessionID, CheckpointID, transcript position (`internal/cli/distill_cmd.go:1133`).
- Anchors cross the wire. `SanitizeForEgress` removes only the local transcript path and line; SessionID, Commit, CheckpointID, and TurnID stay in the synced blob (`internal/factsync/egress.go`).
- Brainstore currently drops anchors when it projects the blob into `brain_facts` rows.
- The platform already maps checkpoints and sessions to trails. Trails have stable ULIDs.
- The client has the full commit graph. Reachability (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`) is a cheap local check. The server does not need the git graph for anything in this design.

## Design

One rule everywhere: a fact is selected by its anchors, never by a branch name.

### Storage (brainstore)

Per-fact rows keyed `(repo_id, fact_id)`, plus anchor rows (fact_id → SessionID, CheckpointID, Commit, TurnID). No set heads, no CAS, no `branch` column in any key. Branch may be stored as display metadata on an anchor.

Writes are idempotent upserts: anchors union, status advances one way, text/paths are fixed by the content-derived ID. Two clients upserting the same fact converge without coordination. Conflicting facts (two active facts that disagree) are stored side by side; resolution belongs to the planned async pipeline, same as before.

### Sync protocol (replaces `facts?branch=` / `facts/advance`)

- **Push:** `POST /repos/{id}/brain/facts:upsert` with a batch of facts + anchors. Idempotent. Server stamps attribution from the token, as today.
- **Pull:** `GET /repos/{id}/brain/facts?since=<cursor>` — a repo-wide delta feed ordered by `updated_at`, paginated. No branch parameter.
- **Client-side filter on pull:** keep a fact if any anchor commit is reachable from local HEAD, or any anchor session is one of this member's sessions, or the fact has no session/commit anchors (repo pool). Everything else is cached or skipped per client policy.

The old protocol and `factmerge`'s set-level CAS/merge path are retired. The e2e-validation condition for replacing the protocol was met on 2026-10-08, and exposure is still off behind `trail-memories`, so the replacement cost is at its minimum now.

### Why rename, delete, recycle, and merge stop being cases at all

- Rename/delete: no storage is keyed by the name, so there is nothing to strand or orphan.
- Recycle: the new branch's history does not contain the old trail's commits, so the old facts fail the pull filter. If the old trail merged, its commits are in the new branch's history and its facts pass the filter — which is correct, not contamination.
- Merge: the trail's commits become ancestors of main. From that moment the facts pass every main-based filter: the repo Memories page and every teammate's pull on main. No promote event, no copy.
- Closed without merge: the commits never reach main, so the facts never pass a main-based filter. They remain visible on the closed trail.
- A lost event delays an upload. It cannot misplace a fact, because selection is computed from stored anchors at read time.

### Attachment (which trail or page shows a fact)

- A fact belongs to trail T if any anchor references a session, checkpoint, or commit in T. The UI renders the fact next to the commit its anchor points to.
- A fact appears on the repo Memories page if its anchoring commits are reachable from the default branch, or if it has no session/commit anchors (the repo pool).

| Situation | Anchors present | Where the fact shows |
|---|---|---|
| Work on a trail branch | session + checkpoint + commit | on the trail, next to its commit |
| Distilled at session end, after the last commit | session + last checkpoint | on the trail, via session membership |
| Detached HEAD | session + checkpoint | wherever those commits end up |
| Work directly on main | session + checkpoint on main | repo page |
| Authored mid-session, before any commit | session | attaches when the session's commits/trail exist; until then, repo pool |
| `remember` outside any session | author + timestamp only | repo pool |

### Local store

The branch directories become a cache of the pull filter's output plus this machine's own unsynced facts. Brief/recall read them as today. Because the cache rebuilds from HEAD reachability, branch rename and recycle need no local detection: the view for the current checkout is always derivable. The previously planned `lineage.json` mechanism is not needed. The local refactor can be staged: first point the pull path at the new protocol and keep writing branch directories; later collapse the directories into a single store with reachability views.

### Upload triggers

- Checkpoint event (per commit). This is the main trigger and the reason facts appear on the trail during review rather than after it. The plugin endpoint `entire brain memory notify --event checkpoint` exists on main (`internal/cli/memory_cmd.go`). The host-side caller (`brainnotify`, entireio/cli commit 73a92e8da) is on the unmerged branch `feat/brain-lifecycle-hints`. COR-2127 lands the host side and wires the checkpoint event to a throttled sync.
- Session-end hook, daemon tick, and connect stay. They cover facts with no commit and act as reconciliation if an event is missed.
- Expected staleness: seconds after a commit or session end; at most one daemon tick otherwise.

## Implementation tickets

1. COR-2123 — brainstore: per-fact storage (`(repo_id, fact_id)` + anchor rows), upsert and delta-feed endpoints, migration that explodes existing branch heads into per-fact rows with anchors, then drops the head tables.
2. COR-2124 — the attachment join: fact anchors → trail membership, and the main-reachability predicate for the repo page. Includes deciding where the join runs (see open questions).

5. COR-2127 — host `brainnotify` + plugin checkpoint-event sync trigger.

1. Anchor precision. Distill stamps every fact of a session with the session's latest checkpoint. Measure anchor quality on prod data before building per-commit rendering.
2. Where the trail join runs. Options: the BFF joins at read time (it already holds trail membership; brainstore stores facts with anchors and nothing else), core pushes a checkpoint→trail membership projection into brainstore, or brainstore queries core. 3. Repo pool UX. How authored facts with no anchors appear on the repo page. The first version of the page can hide them.

**Design v3 — anchors everywhere, per-fact sync. Approved 2026-10-14. This comment is the canonical design; v1 (scope/alias) and v2 (anchor attachment, branch-head transport) are summarized at the end.**

## Summary

A fact records which session, checkpoint, and commit produced it. These provenance anchors are written at creation and never change. Every consumer — the trail page, the repo Memories page, and a teammate's local brain — selects facts by querying these anchors. The branch name is not a key anywhere. Sync is per-fact: the client upserts facts up, and pulls a repo-wide delta down, filtered locally by git reachability from its own HEAD. Upload runs on the checkpoint event (per commit), on session end, and on the daemon tick.

## Facts about the current system the design uses

- Fact identity is `sha256(normalized text + sorted paths)`; branch is not part of it. Status moves one way (active → superseded/retracted).
- Distill stamps each fact with SessionID + CheckpointID anchors; anchors cross the wire (`SanitizeForEgress` strips only the local transcript path/line). Brainstore currently drops them when projecting rows.
- The platform already maps checkpoints and sessions to trails.
- The client has the full commit graph; reachability is a cheap local check. The server never needs the git graph.

## Storage (brainstore)

Per-fact rows keyed `(repo_id, fact_id)` plus anchor rows (SessionID, CheckpointID, Commit, TurnID). No set heads, no CAS, no branch in any key. Writes are idempotent upserts: anchors union, status advances one way, text/paths are fixed by the content-derived ID. Conflicting facts are stored side by side; resolution stays deferred to the async pipeline.

## Sync protocol (replaces `facts?branch=` / `facts/advance`)

- Push: `POST /repos/{id}/brain/facts:upsert`, batch, idempotent, server-stamped attribution.
- Pull: `GET /repos/{id}/brain/facts?since=<cursor>` — repo-wide delta feed, paginated, no branch parameter.
- Client filter on pull: keep a fact if any anchor commit is reachable from local HEAD, or any anchor session belongs to this member, or the fact has no session/commit anchors (repo pool).

The e2e condition for replacing the protocol was met 2026-10-08 and exposure is off behind `trail-memories`, so the replacement cost is at its minimum now.

## Why the failure cases stop existing

- Rename/delete: no storage is keyed by the name; nothing strands.
- Recycle: the new branch's history does not contain the old trail's commits, so old facts fail the pull filter. If the old trail merged, they pass — which is correct, not contamination.
- Merge: the trail's commits become ancestors of main, so its facts pass every main-based filter — the repo page and every teammate's pull. No promote step. (v2 had a hole here: per-branch heads without promote meant a teammate on main never received merged facts locally.)
- Closed without merge: the commits never reach main; the facts stay visible only on the closed trail.
- A lost event delays an upload. It cannot misplace a fact; selection is computed from stored anchors at read time.

## Attachment

- A fact belongs to trail T if any anchor references a session, checkpoint, or commit in T; rendered next to the anchoring commit.
- Repo Memories page: facts whose anchor commits are reachable from the default branch, plus the repo pool.

| Situation | Anchors present | Where the fact shows |
|---|---|---|
| Work on a trail branch | session + checkpoint + commit | on the trail, next to its commit |
| Distilled at session end, after the last commit | session + last checkpoint | on the trail, via session membership |
| Detached HEAD | session + checkpoint | wherever those commits end up |
| Work directly on main | session + checkpoint on main | repo page |
| Authored mid-session, before any commit | session | attaches when the session's commits/trail exist; until then, repo pool |
| `remember` outside any session | author + timestamp only | repo pool |

## Local store

Branch directories become a cache of the pull filter's output plus this machine's own unsynced facts; brief/recall read them unchanged. The view rebuilds from HEAD reachability, so branch rename/recycle need no local detection — `lineage.json` is cancelled. Collapsing the directories into a single store with reachability views can be a later stage.

## Upload triggers

- Checkpoint event (per commit), the main trigger. Plugin endpoint `entire brain memory notify --event checkpoint` is on main; the host caller (`brainnotify`, entireio/cli 73a92e8da) is on the unmerged branch `feat/brain-lifecycle-hints`. COR-2127 lands both.
- Session-end hook, daemon tick, connect stay — they cover facts with no commit and reconcile missed events.
- Staleness: seconds after a commit or session end; at most one daemon tick otherwise.

## Tickets

1. COR-2123 — brainstore per-fact storage + anchors, upsert + delta endpoints, migration from heads.
2. COR-2124 — attachment join (anchors → trail membership; main-reachability predicate) + join-location decision.
3. COR-2125 — trail UI beside commits + repo Memories page, behind `trail-memories`.
4. COR-2126 — plugin per-fact push + reachability-filtered pull; lineage.json cancelled.
5. COR-2127 — host `brainnotify` + checkpoint-event sync trigger.

## Open questions

1. Anchor precision: distill stamps a session's latest checkpoint — right trail, not always the right commit within it; TurnID is the upgrade. Measure prod anchor quality before per-commit rendering.
2. Where the trail join runs: BFF read-time (lean), core-pushed membership projection, or brainstore querying core.
3. Repo pool UX: first version of the page can hide anchor-less facts.
4. Delta-feed scale: fine at thousands of facts; define pagination + cursor-reset resync up front.

## Superseded versions

**V1 (scope/alias):** set heads re-keyed by server-resolved scope (trail ULID / repo-default / anon+generation), alias table from trail lifecycle events, promote-on-merge. Replaced: the machinery reconstructs through events what anchors state directly, and events can be lost or reordered.

**V2 (anchor attachment, branch-head transport):** anchor joins for attachment, but kept branch-named heads with a recycle lineage marker and local `lineage.json`. Replaced: the marker patches a key that no longer needs to exist, and per-branch heads without promote break teammate distribution of merged facts.

Decisions that hold across all versions: merged trails' facts become repo-visible automatically; closed-unmerged trails' facts never do; the repo page does not show work-in-progress branch facts; conflict resolution stays deferred to the async pipeline.

Answered above, and the gap is now recorded in all three places: the `.context` doc, COR-2126 (as an explicit prerequisite bullet — stamp `Anchor.Commit` at distill), and the shared artifact doc.

Short version again: **authored facts carry a commit SHA** (HEAD, or the named branch's tip, resolved at `remember` time); **distilled facts don't** — they carry SessionID + CheckpointID only, and the commit is reachable only through the platform's checkpoint→commit mapping. Since distilled facts are ~98% of the store and v3's pull filter and repo-page predicate both test commit reachability, distill stamping the checkpoint's commit at creation is now a prerequisite in COR-2126 — one write at creation, pure git on every read, works offline.
do we actually need the distill path? what is teh downside of just having one interface (remember) for the memories

Distill isn't needed for the v3 design to work — attachment and sync are indifferent to how a fact was created. Whether to keep it is a product question about coverage, and the data in this repo's own brain is the argument on both sides.

**What remember-only buys you.** A much smaller system: `distill_cmd.go` and its pipeline (chunking, per-session caching, agent failure handling, flush logic, backfill) go away, along with the token spend per session and the dependency on a configured coding agent. Every fact gets written at the moment someone decided it mattered, so precision is high and the anchor problem disappears — `remember` already stamps the commit; the COR-2126 prerequisite would be unnecessary.

**The downside, concretely:**

1. **Coverage collapses to agent discipline.** This repo's brain: 2,404 distilled facts, 45 authored — explicit capture produced ~2% of the volume, in a repo whose agent-guide *mandates* recording facts. Agents forget, sessions end under context pressure, and humans essentially never author. Every harness (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot) needs its own instruction to call remember; distill needs none — it captures from any transcript the platform already has.
2. **The trail-memories launch feature goes mostly empty.** "Reviewer sees the decisions and gotchas recorded while building" only works if the builder's agent remembered to record them. At a 2% capture rate, most trails show nothing.
3. **No backfill.** Distill processed 255 historical sessions here. Remember can only capture forward.
4. **Selection bias.** The agent records what it *thinks* mattered mid-task. Gotchas often only look important in hindsight — a later session recalling "we tried X and it failed" depends on capture the first session had no reason to prioritize.

**The honest framing:** distill is the floor (automatic, full coverage, mediocre precision), remember is the ceiling (precise, sparse). Remember-only keeps the ceiling and removes the floor.

Two things before deciding:

- The real question is whether distilled facts are *good*, not whether there are many — 2,404 mediocre facts could be recall noise that buries the 45 good ones. That's empirical, and the memory-ladder bench harness (merged as #336) exists to measure exactly this. Running it with distilled-only vs authored-only vs both would replace this debate with a number.
- There's a cheaper middle: keep both but rank them. `Origin` already distinguishes distilled from authored, and records have a `Confidence` field — brief/recall and the trail UI can weight authored facts above distilled ones, so distill's noise cost drops without losing its coverage. Lazier than deleting a working pipeline, and reversible once the bench data says which way to go.

My recommendation: don't remove distill on intuition — run the ladder comparison, and in the meantime treat authored > distilled as a ranking signal rather than an either/or.

3. **Distill stays as-is.** Ingestion is one funnel: `remember` and distill both write the local fact store; the store pushes to brainstore on post-commit; every view selects by anchors.

name: entire-brain-distill
description: Distill captured Entire session turns into durable repository facts under a strict quality gate. Rendered with the active taxonomy block and run over exported session transcripts by `entire brain distill`. Default output is nothing.
---

You are an expert note-taker for software-development work. You read conversation
turns between a human and an AI coding agent and extract **durable facts** that
will help a future session — a returning human or a fresh agent — quickly
rebuild the context needed to keep working on this repository.

Think like a senior engineer writing onboarding notes: capture the *why*, the
*intent*, the *implicit conventions*, and the *decisions* that are not visible
from reading the code or git history. Capture project context (stack, tooling,
CI/CD, standards), workflow rules (branching, testing, review), user preferences
that affect how work should be done, and non-obvious constraints.

################################################################
# THE SILENT DEFAULT — READ THIS BEFORE WRITING ANYTHING       #
################################################################
Your default answer is NOTHING. Empty output. Zero lines.

The large majority of turns contain no durable facts and MUST produce no output.
Emitting nothing is the correct, expected, high-quality result for most turns —
it is not a failure, it is the baseline. A silent turn means the session stayed
focused on ephemeral work, which is normal and good.

Output at least one line ONLY if you can honestly answer YES to all four:

  1. DURABLE — still relevant a week or a month from now?
  2. USEFUL — would a future session genuinely benefit, or is it obvious?
  3. NOT ALREADY KNOWN — not discoverable from the code, git log, README, or
     existing brain seed context?
  4. WORTH WRITING DOWN — would a senior engineer record this in onboarding
     notes, or roll their eyes at it?

If any answer is no, unsure, or "maybe" — DO NOT emit a line. Err strongly
toward silence. A missed fact will be captured on a later turn when it actually
matters; a bogus or trivial fact pollutes the brain permanently.

ALWAYS-CAPTURE TRIGGERS (override the silent default — if any fire, emit a line):
  - Standing rules / going-forward instructions: "from now on…", "going
    forward…", "always X", "never X", "we should/must…", "make sure to…",
    "every time…", "whenever…".
  - Stated preferences about how the user wants to work or how code should be
    written: "I prefer…", "use X over Y", "don't use…".
  - Architectural / design / tooling decisions resolved THIS turn — capture the
    *why*, not just the *what*. Skip in-flight discussions the user defers
    ("TBD", "pending review", "haven't landed on it yet", "come back to it").
  - Project facts surfaced this turn that are not already in the code or seed
    context (stack choices, infra, branching, ownership, hard constraints).
  - Non-obvious technical knowledge: invariants, gotchas, hidden constraints,
    performance characteristics a future session would re-learn the hard way.
  - QUESTIONS SETTLED NEGATIVELY — the highest-value capture of all. A design
    that was rejected, an approach that was tried and failed, an experiment
    that measured no effect, a tuning knob shown to be a non-lever ("we tried
    X and it didn't work because Y", "X measured within noise", "decided NOT
    to do X because Z"). Future sessions re-explore dead ends unless told;
    capture WHAT was tried, WHY it failed or was rejected (the evidence), and
    WHEN it would be worth revisiting — all in the fact text.

When a trigger fires, the four checks above still apply as a sanity filter, not
a high bar. Standing rules and stated preferences pass by definition.

Turns that should almost always produce NOTHING:
  - Routine Q&A (asked and answered, nothing persistent learned).
  - Code reads, file exploration, "show me X" requests.
  - One-off debugging that resolved within the turn.
  - Tool calls and their outputs (mechanics, not facts).
  - Restatements of things already in code, seed context, or git history.
  - "thanks" / "ok" / "keep going" / feedback that applies only to this turn.

## Output Format

When — and only when — you have a fact that passes all four checks, output ONE
line per fact in exactly this format:

    <kind><TAB><taxonomy-path>[,<taxonomy-path>]<TAB><fact>

The leading <kind> is exactly ONE of these six words — the *shape* of the claim,
independent of its topic:

content.text:
Here's exactly what a background distill pass does, start to finish.

**What triggers it and what it selects.** Three callers funnel into the same `runDistill`, serialized by a per-brain pass lock so two runs never spend tokens on the same sessions: the session-end hook (incremental — just the session that ended), the watch daemon's distill step (off by default; when enabled it runs at most once per `--distill-every` and caps how many undistilled sessions one pass takes), and a human running `entire brain distill` (or the detached setup backfill, which is how the 255 historical sessions here got processed). The input inventory is the brain's session manifest — the exported transcripts the plugin already keeps per branch, not live agent state.

**What it skips.** Before any model call, each session's transcript is fingerprinted. A per-session cache (salted with the rendered prompt, the agent name, the confidence threshold — so changing any of those invalidates it) skips sessions whose fingerprint is unchanged. A steady-state pass over an already-distilled repo costs zero tokens.

**What it processes.** Each new session's transcript is preprocessed and split into chunks of at most 48 KB (`--max-chunk-bytes`), line-numbered. Up to 4 chunks are in flight at once (`--concurrency`).

**The model call.** Per chunk, it shells out to a coding-agent CLI in a locked-down one-shot mode:
- `--agent auto` (the default) picks whatever is on PATH: codex first, then claude — there is no baked-in model; `--model` / `--effort` pin one (e.g. the watch daemon runs the cheap model), otherwise the CLI's default applies. `ollama` and a custom `command` argv are also supported; no-egress mode forces none and distill refuses to run.
- The invocation is deliberately inert: for claude-code it's `claude --print --tools "" --no-session-persistence --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{}}' --permission-mode dontAsk --system-prompt <prompt>`; for codex, `codex exec --ephemeral --sandbox read-only --ignore-user-config`. No tools, no MCP, no filesystem — pure text in, text out.
- The **system prompt** is `templates/entire-brain-distill.md` with the repo's fact taxonomy substituted in. Its core instruction is a strict quality gate: *the default output is nothing* — emit a fact only if it's durable, useful, not already discoverable from code/git/README, and worth writing in onboarding notes; with always-capture triggers for standing rules, stated preferences, resolved decisions with their why, and (highest value) questions settled negatively — rejected designs and failed attempts.
- The **input** on stdin is the line-numbered chunk. The expected output is zero or more lines of `kind<TAB>taxonomy-path[,path]<TAB>fact text`, capped per chunk; malformed or over-cap lines are dropped.

**What happens to the output.** Each emitted line becomes a `factmerge.Record`: ID = sha256 of normalized text + sorted paths (so re-distilling is idempotent — the same statement dedupes to the same fact), anchored with the session ID, the session's latest checkpoint, and the transcript line it came from. A second agent call — the **reconcile** prompt — decides whether a new fact merges with or supersedes an existing one; above the confidence threshold the decision auto-applies, below it the pair is queued as a proposal for human review. Results flush incrementally (including on failure streaks, so a killed run keeps what it extracted), and a misconfigured agent aborts fast after a few consecutive failures instead of churning through every session.

So concretely, "a distill job running in the background" means: take the transcripts of sessions that ended since the last pass, skip the unchanged ones, split the rest into ~48 KB chunks, run each chunk through a tool-less one-shot codex/claude call whose system prompt is a note-taker with a strong bias toward emitting nothing, parse the tab-separated fact lines, dedupe by content hash, anchor to session + checkpoint, and merge into the branch's `facts.ndjson` — with ambiguous merges parked for review.

content.text:
From the Entire **checkpoints in git** — the plugin never reads the agent harness's own session files. The chain:

1. **Capture (host CLI, at commit).** When you commit, the host CLI's git hooks capture the AI session as a checkpoint; the transcript is stored as blobs under the checkpoint ref in the repo's git object store (and reaches the platform via the normal push).
2. **Export (plugin, into the brain dir).** The brain's export step materializes those transcripts into its own directory, one `.jsonl` per session under `sessions/branches/<branch>/`, and records them in the session manifest (SessionID, branch, LatestCheckpoint, TranscriptPath). It gets the content one of two ways:
   - shelling out to the host: `entire checkpoint explain --transcript --session-index <n> <checkpointID>` (`internal/cli/export.go:3010`), or
   - the snapshot path: reading transcript blobs directly out of the checkpoint ref with git cat-file (`checkpointBlobReader`), no host CLI call — this is what lets backfill process history, and a blob missing in a partial clone is skipped with a warning rather than failing the export.
3. **Distill reads the exported files.** The pass iterates the manifest's sessions and reads each `TranscriptPath` from the brain dir — never from `~/.claude` or any harness state.

One consequence worth noting for the design: distill's input *comes from* checkpoints, so a session that never produced a checkpoint (never committed) has no exported transcript and never gets distilled. That's why effectively every distilled fact has a CheckpointID — and why the checkpoint event is such a natural sync trigger: the same moment that creates distill's input also creates the commit the resulting facts will anchor to.

Yes — there's a full plaintext copy on disk, made by the export step (not distill itself). On this machine: `~/.local/share/entire/plugins/data/brain/repos/gh/entireio/entire-brain/sessions/branches/<branch-slug>/<timestamp>_<agent>_<sessionID>_<checkpoint>.jsonl` — **1.5 GB of transcript copies** for this repo alone.

How it works:

- Export reads each transcript out of the checkpoint ref (via `entire checkpoint explain --transcript` or direct git cat-file) and writes it as a plain `.jsonl` file into the brain dir, tracked in the session manifest.
- An export cursor makes it incremental — unchanged sessions are reused, not re-extracted from git.
- `cleanupStaleSessionFiles` garbage-collects transcripts the manifest no longer claims.
- Distill (and recall's evidence spans, and conversation indexing) then read those files; git stays the source of truth, the brain dir is a derived cache.

So the data exists twice locally: once as checkpoint blobs in the git object store, once as flat files in the plugin data dir. The duplication buys cheap line-addressed reads (distill chunks by line, recall cites `transcript:line` anchors) without shelling out to git per access — but it is why the brain dir gets big, and it's a thing to keep in mind for the blob-GC work (COR-2037 covers the server side; the local cache has its own growth path).

input.title: entire-brain: bound the exported transcript cache (full plaintext copy of every session transcript)
input.description:
The brain's export step copies every session transcript out of the git checkpoint refs into flat files under the plugin data dir (`sessions/branches/<branch>/<ts>_<agent>_<session>_<checkpoint>.jsonl`), tracked by the session manifest. The data exists twice locally: once as checkpoint blobs in the git object store, once as plaintext files. On the entire-brain repo this cache is **1.5 GB** and grows without bound.

The copies exist for cheap line-addressed reads: distill chunks by line, recall cites `transcript:line` evidence anchors, and conversation indexing reads the same files. Git stays the source of truth, so the cache is rebuildable — eviction is always safe.

Fix options (owner's choice; requirements below):

1. **Bounded cache with eviction**: keep recent/undistilled sessions materialized, evict by age/size, re-materialize on demand from the checkpoint ref (the export path already knows how). Smallest behavior change.
2. **Compress at rest** (e.g. zstd per file): transcripts compress well; decompress on read. Cheapest to build, cuts the footprint but not the duplication.
3. **Read from git on demand, no persistent copies**: `git cat-file` per access. Largest change — distill, recall evidence spans, and conversation indexing all read these paths today.

Requirements regardless of option:
- Distill's incremental fingerprint/cache keeps working (a re-materialized transcript must fingerprint identically).
- Recall's `transcript:line` anchors stay resolvable — re-materialization must be deterministic, or anchor resolution must learn the on-demand path.
- Backfill over full history stays possible (it can materialize transiently).
- `cleanupStaleSessionFiles` semantics preserved or subsumed.

Context: found during the COR-2110 design discussion while tracing where distill reads transcripts from.

The ticket states the problem (full plaintext duplicate of every transcript, 1.5 GB here, unbounded), why the copies exist (line-addressed reads for distill chunking, recall's `transcript:line` anchors, conversation indexing), that git is the source of truth so eviction is always safe, and three fix options (bounded cache with re-materialization on demand, compress at rest, read-from-git) with the invariants any option must keep: identical fingerprints on re-materialization, resolvable recall anchors, backfill, and stale-file cleanup.

On your other two points, no changes were needed: the design already names the post-commit hook (checkpoint event) as the sync trigger, and already states distill stays as a feeder — "`remember` and distill both write the local fact store; the store pushes to brainstore on post-commit; every view selects by anchors."

Where everything stands: design v3 is canonical on COR-2110 (doc in `.context`, artifact shared), implementation tickets are COR-2123 (brainstore per-fact store + migration), COR-2124 (attachment join), COR-2125 (UI), COR-2126 (per-fact client + distill commit-stamping), COR-2127 (checkpoint-event trigger), and now COR-2128 (transcript cache) as adjacent cleanup.
okay lets list out the plan then for these changes given our approach. make it concise so i can review it.

**Plan: memories ↔ trails (COR-2110 v3)**

**Model (one rule):** a fact is selected by its anchors (session + checkpoint + commit), never by branch name. `remember` + distill (kept as-is) feed the local fact store; the store pushes to brainstore on post-commit; every view is an anchor query.

**Work, in dependency order:**

1. **COR-2126a — plugin: stamp `Anchor.Commit` at distill.** Distilled facts today carry only SessionID + CheckpointID; the reachability filter needs the commit. Prerequisite for everything below.
2. **COR-2123 — brainstore: per-fact storage.** Rows keyed `(repo_id, fact_id)` + anchor rows; `trail_id` column stamped on trail merge; endpoints `facts:upsert` (idempotent batch) and `facts?since=` (repo-wide delta feed). Migration: explode existing branch heads into per-fact rows, backfill `Anchor.Commit` via core's checkpoint→commit mapping, drop head tables; old branch routes stay behind a shim for a short window.
3. **COR-2126 — plugin: new sync client.** Push = batch upsert on post-commit / session-end / tick / connect. Pull = delta feed + local filter: anchor commit reachable from HEAD, or own session, or merged `trail_id`, or repo pool. Local branch dirs become a cache of the filter output; `lineage.json` cancelled. This also fixes teammate distribution of merged facts — no promote step.
4. **COR-2127 — checkpoint-event trigger.** Land host-side `brainnotify` (stuck on unmerged `feat/brain-lifecycle-hints`) and wire the per-commit hint to a throttled sync.
5. **COR-2124 — attachment join.** Trail page: fact ∈ trail T iff an anchor hits T's sessions/checkpoints/commits, rendered beside the commit. Repo page: main-reachable anchor commits OR merged `trail_id` (squash-merge backlink) OR repo pool. Decide join location (lean: BFF at read time).
6. **COR-2125 — UI.** Trail memories beside commits + repo Memories page, behind `trail-memories`.
7. **COR-2128 — adjacent cleanup.** Bound the local transcript cache (1.5 GB plaintext duplicate of checkpoint data).

**Open questions before 2124/2125:** anchor precision (whole session stamps its latest checkpoint — right trail, coarse per-commit placement; TurnID is the upgrade), join location, repo-pool UX, delta-feed pagination/resync.

**What this kills:** branch keys everywhere, the alias/scope machinery, promote-on-merge events, recycle markers, local rename/recycle detection. Rename/delete/recycle become non-events; merge visibility is derived from reachability + the merge backlink.

let's talk through how this works throughout a trail. for example, im doing work and a fact gets created and i push a commit. that fact goes to the brainstore. then i do more work and another fact adn then another commit. and so on until the trail merges. 

how does this get treated?

Here's the timeline, step by step. Say you're on branch `feat/x`, in session S.

**Commit 1.** You do work; the post-commit hook fires. Three things happen on that beat: the host captures checkpoint cp1 (your transcript so far), the checkpoint event nudges the plugin, and the plugin batch-upserts the fact store to brainstore. At this point the store holds any facts you *authored* so far (`remember` stamps SessionID + HEAD at authoring time). Distilled facts from this session don't exist yet — distill runs at session end. Note the trail may not even exist yet (it's created on your first push); that's fine — brainstore just stores facts with anchors, and attachment is computed at read time, so nothing needs to be re-homed when the trail appears.

**Trail created (first push).** A reviewer opens trail T. The trail page asks: which facts have an anchor in T's membership (sessions, checkpoints cp1…, commits c1…)? Your fact anchored to c1 shows up beside commit c1. No event moved anything — the query just started matching.

**Commit 2, 3, ….** Same loop: each post-commit sync upserts the whole active set — new facts insert, already-synced facts no-op (idempotent by content ID). Each authored fact anchors to the HEAD at the moment you remembered it, so it renders beside that commit.

**Session ends.** Distill reads the session's exported transcript, extracts facts, anchors them to S + the session's **latest** checkpoint (+ its commit), and the session-end sync uploads them. They appear on the trail beside the last commit — this is the precision coarseness we flagged: a fact learned around c1 but distilled at session end clusters at c3. Right trail always; right commit only as good as the anchors (TurnID is the upgrade path).

**Meanwhile, teammates.** Their pulls receive your facts in the delta feed but their filter drops them: c1…c3 aren't reachable from their HEAD and it's not their session. Your WIP facts pollute nobody's brief. A teammate who checks out `feat/x` passes the filter and gets them. The repo Memories page doesn't show them either — not main-reachable, trail not merged.

**You retract a fact mid-trail.** Next sync upserts `status=retracted`; the trail page shows it retracted (or hides it). One-way, everywhere.

**Trail merges.** Two sub-cases, same outcome:
- *True merge:* c1…c3 become main ancestors. Instantly, with no event: the repo page predicate passes, and every teammate's next pull on main passes the reachability filter — your facts land in their local stores and start appearing in brief/recall.
- *Squash merge:* the commits are rewritten, reachability fails — the trail-merge event stamps `trail_id = T` on facts whose anchors match T, and repo page + pull filter treat a merged `trail_id` as main-visible.

The trail page itself never changes: anchors are immutable, so trail T shows its memories beside its commits forever — through branch deletion, name recycling, anything.

**One real edge this walkthrough exposes:** a fact that arrives *after* the merge event — your session ends after the squash merge, distill uploads a fact anchored to cp3/c3 — misses the merge-time `trail_id` stamp, and with squashed commits it would be invisible on the repo page. The fix is to also stamp on upsert: when a fact arrives whose anchors belong to an already-merged trail, stamp `trail_id` then. (Pure read-time joins don't have this problem; only the materialized stamp does.) Adding that to COR-2123 now.

### Upload triggers

The checkpoint event (post-commit hook) is the primary trigger for both distill and sync. Session-end is being deprecated — developers leave sessions running for days, so it fires late or never. Nothing new may depend on it.

- **Event plumbing**: the host CLI's post-commit git hook (installed by `entire enable`) captures the checkpoint, then calls `brainnotify.Notify`, which spawns a detached `entire brain memory notify --event checkpoint --session <id>` through the plugin dispatcher. The plugin records the hint and nudges its worker; the worker runs a throttled distill + fact sync. Detached and never-fails: a missing or broken plugin cannot affect the commit. COR-2127 lands both.

- **Daemon tick** stays as reconciliation for missed events and for facts with no commit; **connect** stays for first contact. The session-end hook keeps working until removed but is not load-bearing.
- The trigger is transport-agnostic: before COR-2123/2126 land it fires the existing branch-head sync; after, the upsert/pull client. COR-2127 does not depend on the storage rework.
- Expected staleness: seconds after a commit; at most one daemon tick otherwise.

input.title: Checkpoint event: host brainnotify → plugin, primary trigger for distill + fact sync
input.description:
Part of the COR-2110 design (v3). The checkpoint event becomes the **primary** trigger for both distill and fact sync. Session-end is being deprecated (developers leave sessions running for days, so it fires late or never); nothing new may depend on it.

**Where the event comes from and how it is triggered:**

1. `entire enable` installs a post-commit git hook that runs `entire hooks git post-commit` — this is the existing checkpoint-capture path in the host CLI.
2. Inside that flow the host calls `brainnotify.Notify`, which spawns a detached `entire brain memory notify --event checkpoint --session <id>` through the plugin dispatcher. Detached and never-fails by design: a missing or broken plugin cannot affect the commit or the hook's output. This host half exists on the **unmerged** entireio/cli branch `feat/brain-lifecycle-hints` (commit 73a92e8da) — land or re-cut it.
3. The plugin endpoint (`entire brain memory notify`, on main in `internal/cli/memory_cmd.go`) records a content-free hint and nudges the plugin's worker.
4. The worker runs, throttled: distill the transcript delta since the previous checkpoint (anchoring facts to the checkpoint window they came from — better precision than session-end distill, which lumps the whole session onto its last checkpoint), then push the fact store.

**Interaction with COR-2123/2126:** none structurally — the trigger is transport-agnostic. Before the per-fact storage/client land, the hint fires the existing branch-head sync; after COR-2126, it fires the upsert/pull client. This ticket can land first.

Daemon tick stays as reconciliation for missed events and commit-less facts; connect stays for first contact; the session-end hook keeps working until removed but is not load-bearing.

input.title: entire-brain: remove the local transcript cache — read transcripts from git on demand
input.description:
Decided on COR-2110 review: no local transcript cache at all. The git repo already holds every transcript as checkpoint blobs; the plugin should extract on demand instead of duplicating storage.

Today the export step copies every session transcript out of the git checkpoint refs into flat files under the plugin data dir (`sessions/branches/<branch>/<ts>_<agent>_<session>_<checkpoint>.jsonl`) — **1.5 GB on the entire-brain repo**, unbounded growth, a full plaintext duplicate of data git already stores.

Change: distill, recall evidence anchors (`transcript:line`), and conversation indexing read transcripts from the checkpoint refs on demand (`git cat-file` / the `checkpointBlobReader` path that the snapshot export already uses). Transient materialization is allowed where a pass needs a file on disk (e.g. backfill), deleted when the pass ends.

Requirements:
- Distill's incremental fingerprint cache keeps working — an on-demand read must fingerprint identically to the old exported file.
- Recall's `transcript:line` anchors stay resolvable — anchor resolution learns the on-demand path (extraction must be deterministic so line offsets hold).
- Backfill over full history stays possible.
- Migration deletes the existing cache; the session manifest keeps session metadata (IDs, branch, checkpoint) without materialized `TranscriptPath` files.
- A partial clone with promisor-absent blobs degrades the same way it does today (skip with a warning).

content.text:
All five comments are folded into the doc and tickets. The updated plan:

**Model:** a fact is selected by its provenance anchors (session + checkpoint + commit), never by branch name. `remember` + distill both feed the local fact store; the store pushes to brainstore on the post-commit (checkpoint) event; every view is an anchor query.

**Anchor rule (your #1):** distill stamps the commit resolved from the fact's **own checkpoint** via the `Entire-Checkpoint` commit trailer — the entity index already builds this mapping from git log. Never HEAD; an unresolvable checkpoint leaves the commit blank. A background distill of an old session therefore anchors to that session's historical commit.

**Trigger (your #3, #4):** the checkpoint event is the primary trigger for **both distill and sync**; session-end is deprecated and nothing new depends on it. Plumbing: the post-commit git hook (installed by `entire enable`) captures the checkpoint → host calls `brainnotify.Notify` → detached `entire brain memory notify --event checkpoint` into the plugin → throttled worker distills the delta since the previous checkpoint, then pushes. Detached, never-fails, can't touch the commit. Transport-agnostic, so it can land before the storage rework. Bonus: per-checkpoint distill anchors facts to the right checkpoint window, improving the precision problem.

**Work, in order:**

1. **COR-2127** — land host `brainnotify` (stuck on unmerged `feat/brain-lifecycle-hints`) + wire the checkpoint event to throttled distill + sync. No dependencies; can go first.
2. **COR-2126a** — distill stamps `Anchor.Commit` from the fact's checkpoint (trailer mapping, never HEAD, blank if unresolvable).
3. **COR-2123** — brainstore per-fact storage: `(repo_id, fact_id)` + anchor rows; `trail_id` stamped at trail merge **and** on late upserts whose anchors belong to an already-merged trail; `facts:upsert` + `facts?since=` delta feed; migration explodes branch heads and backfills commits via checkpoint→commit; old routes behind a shim briefly.
4. **COR-2126** — plugin per-fact client: batch-upsert push; delta pull filtered locally by HEAD reachability / own session / merged `trail_id` / repo pool. Fixes teammate distribution with no promote step; `lineage.json` cancelled.
5. **COR-2124** — attachment join: trail page = anchors ∩ trail membership, beside the commit; repo page = main-reachable OR merged `trail_id` OR repo pool. Decide join location (lean: BFF read-time).
6. **COR-2125** — trail UI + repo Memories page, behind `trail-memories`.
7. **COR-2128** — **no local transcript cache**: delete the 1.5 GB plaintext copies; distill/recall/indexing read from the git checkpoint refs on demand (`checkpointBlobReader` path), transient materialization only for backfill; fingerprints and `transcript:line` anchors must survive the switch.

**Still open:** join location (2124), repo-pool UX, delta-feed pagination/resync shape, and measuring real anchor precision on prod data before building per-commit rendering.

content.text:
Checked: your assumption doesn't hold today — **authored facts get a commit-only anchor, no session ID**, even when an agent calls `remember` (`facts_write_cmd.go:142` builds the anchor with just `Commit`). Distilled facts always have a session ID. Here's where that leaves each open item:

**1. Repo pool — mostly agree, and it's smaller than it sounded.** Since `remember` stamps HEAD, authored facts attach via their commit like everything else. The pool is only: facts where commit resolution failed (empty repo, unresolvable `--branch`) — rare degenerate cases. So yes: no special UX, they're ordinary rows with null session/checkpoint/commit columns, sorted by recency with the rest. Two follow-ups from your "agent → session id" point: (a) `remember` should stamp the session ID when one is available — the harness hooks know it, so a `--session` flag + env fallback that agents/MCP pass through is a small addition (I'd fold it into COR-2126's stamping prerequisite); (b) note the inverse isn't enforceable — a human running `remember` in a terminal legitimately has no session, so null stays a valid state.

**2. Join location.** Recommendation: **BFF at read time**, with one asymmetry.
- *Trail page*: trivial — the BFF already holds the trail's membership (sessions, checkpoints, commits: bounded lists, tens of items), and brainstore adds one query shape: facts by anchor values (`IN` lists). No projection, no events.
- *Repo page*: the predicate "anchor commit reachable from default" needs the commit graph, which core owns, not brainstore or the BFF. But core already knows which commits are on the default branch (it ingests refs per push). So the repo page is: facts with `trail_id ∈ merged trails` ∪ facts whose anchor commit core marks as on-default ∪ the (near-empty) pool. That's a core-side check over brainstore candidates, not a graph walk.

Investigation done — the plan for COR-2127 has one real scope decision in it, so here it is before I write code:

**What I found:**

1. **Host side (entireio/cli):** the stale branch splits cleanly. Only `brainnotify/` (60 lines + tests) and the call sites matter; the rest of `feat/brain-lifecycle-hints` is unrelated checkpoint-discovery work. The checkpoint call site is `ManualCommitStrategy.PostCommit` — it fires the hint only for sessions that actually condensed into the new checkpoint, which is exactly right. I'd re-cut just that onto current main and wire **only the checkpoint event** (dropping the session-start/end call sites — session-end is deprecated).
2. **Plugin sync on checkpoint:** cheap and safe. `memory notify --event checkpoint` already records a hint and launches the worker; adding a throttled `hostedFactsSyncAndPull` there (propose: 60s min interval via timestamp file, same pattern as the watch throttle) is a small contained change.
3. **Plugin distill on checkpoint — the catch:** distill's cache is a **whole-session fingerprint** (`distill_cmd.go:1961`). A growing session re-runs *every* chunk on each distill, so naively distilling per commit is quadratic in tokens over a long session. The fix is natural though: chunks are split from the start of the transcript, so an appending transcript keeps earlier chunk boundaries stable — a **per-chunk cache** (keyed by chunk content hash) makes per-commit distill re-process only the new tail chunk. Bonus: tail chunks distilled at checkpoint time anchor to the *current* checkpoint, which is precisely the anchor-precision improvement the design promised.

**Proposed split:**
- **A** — cli: new branch, re-cut `brainnotify` + checkpoint call site + tests, PR to entireio/cli.
- **B** — plugin: checkpoint hint → throttled facts sync (60s), PR to entire-brain.
- **C** — plugin: per-chunk distill cache, then enable distill-on-checkpoint. Without C, I'd wire the trigger but leave distill on tick/session-end to avoid the quadratic spend.

The scope question: **do C inside COR-2127** (complete the ticket as designed, ~the largest of the three parts), or ship A+B now and split C into its own ticket? I'd do A+B+C under this ticket since "distill is checkpoint-triggered" is the decision we recorded, but C touches distill's cache model, which you may want as a separately reviewable change.

One logistics note: part A means working in `~/code/entire/cli` directly (new branch off main) — your checkout is clean; say if you'd rather I not touch it.

The cli full-suite build/test run is chugging in the background (big repo — I'll pick up the result when it lands). Meanwhile, your three questions:

**A — the brainnotify mechanism.** It's a detached, content-free re-invocation of the CLI itself. Inside `PostCommit`, after a session actually condenses into the new checkpoint, the host calls `brainnotify.Notify(repoRoot, EventCheckpoint, sessionID, branch)`, which builds the argv `entire brain memory notify --event checkpoint --session <id> --branch <b>` and runs it via `execx.SpawnDetached` — fire-and-forget, no wait, no output read. So: no socket, no queue, no file protocol — the "event bus" is literally spawning the plugin through the host's own plugin dispatcher, carrying only routing metadata (event, session id, branch). Three guards make it safe: it skips when invoked *from* the worker (`ENTIRE_BRAIN_MEMORY_WORKER=1`, loop prevention), it never affects the hook's result (a missing/broken plugin can't touch the commit), and a lost hint costs only freshness because the plugin's reconciliation pass remains authoritative.

**B — "launches the worker" clarified: no, it is not the distill worker.** Today `memory notify` does exactly two things: records the hint in a durable work record, and launches (if not already running, via a coordinator lease) the detached **memory worker** — which only does conversation indexing (transcript → retrieval exchanges). It never distills and never talks to brainstore. Part B adds the missing piece: in the checkpoint-event path, also run a throttled `hostedFactsSyncAndPull` — which pushes whatever facts are *already in the local store* (from earlier distills and `remember`s) to brainstore and pulls the head back. So after B alone: commit → facts already distilled reach brainstore within seconds; facts from the *just-committed* work still wait for the next distill. Part C closes that last gap.

**C — end to end.** Commit → checkpoint cp_n captured → detached notify → plugin (throttled, under the existing distill pass lock): (1) refresh this session's exported transcript, (2) distill it — the new part: the cache entry stores **per-chunk content hashes** alongside the session fingerprint, and since chunks split from the transcript's start, an appended transcript keeps earlier chunks byte-identical — only the new tail chunk(s) miss the cache and hit the model. Facts from those tail chunks anchor to **cp_n** and its commit (the window they actually came from — the precision win). (3) `hostedFactsSyncAndPull` publishes the store. Net cost per commit: roughly one agent call on the new transcript tail instead of re-processing the whole session; a rewritten history (condense/compaction) changes earlier chunk hashes and honestly re-distills them. Edge cases: salt (prompt/model/taxonomy) is part of the chunk hash so config changes invalidate everything, force-rebuild stays session-level, and content-ID dedupe means even a redundant re-distill can't duplicate facts.

The entire-brain plugin currently learns about new work only at session end or on a daemon tick. Developers leave sessions running for days, so facts distilled from a commit's work can reach the trail long after review. This PR gives the plugin a per-commit signal: the moment a session condenses into a checkpoint, the host tells Brain, and Brain can distill + sync on that beat. Part of COR-2127 (hosted memory: checkpoint-event trigger); design on COR-2110.

## What changed

- New \`brainnotify\` package: \`Notify(repoRoot, event, sessionID, branch)\` spawns a detached \`entire brain memory notify --event checkpoint --session <id> --branch <b>\`. Content-free routing metadata only. Skips when invoked from the Brain worker itself (loop prevention), on empty repo/session, or on an unknown event.
- One call site: \`ManualCommitStrategy.PostCommit\` fires the hint per session whose condensation actually produced the checkpoint, keyed on the existing \`condensed\` result.

Never-fails by construction: the spawn is detached, its result is never read, and a missing or broken plugin cannot affect the commit or the hook's output. A lost hint costs freshness only — Brain's reconciliation pass stays authoritative.

Re-cut from \`feat/brain-lifecycle-hints\` (73a92e8da), taking only the brainnotify package and the checkpoint call site. The session-start/end call sites are deliberately not wired: session-end is being deprecated as a Brain trigger.

gh pr create --base main --title "Checkpoint hint triggers throttled distill + hosted fact sync (COR-2127)" --body "## Why

Facts currently reach brainstore only at session end or on a daemon tick, and developers leave sessions running for days — so a trail under review shows no memories from the work being reviewed. The host CLI now sends a detached checkpoint hint per commit (entireio/cli#2784); this PR makes the plugin act on it, so facts appear on the trail during review. Part of COR-2127; design on COR-2110 (v3). Session-end is being deprecated as a trigger and nothing here depends on it.

## What changed

- **\`hostedSyncOnCheckpointHint\`** (\`internal/cli/memory_notify_sync.go\`): on a \`checkpoint\` hint — claim a shared 60s throttle marker under the brain write lock (claim-first, so concurrent detached notifies skip instead of stampeding), then export changed transcripts, distill the hinted session, and run the existing \`hostedFactsSyncAndPull\` for the hinted branch + default branch. Never-fails: every outcome prints to stderr and returns nil; a missing agent still syncs whatever is already in the store.
- **Per-chunk distill cache** (\`distill_cmd.go\`): the cache gains a \`chunks\` map recording each session's salted chunk content hashes. Chunking is prefix-stable, so a transcript grown by one commit re-dispatches only the new tail chunk — per-commit distill is linear in new content, not quadratic in session length — and the tail's facts anchor to the checkpoint that raised the hint. \`--force\` bypasses reuse (it drops the facts it is about to regenerate). Privacy purge clears chunk records alongside session entries. Old cache files load unchanged; reuse starts after their next distill.
- \`memory notify\` wires the \`checkpoint\` event to the above; \`session_start\`/\`session_end\` behavior is unchanged.

## Validation

- New tests: grown transcript re-dispatches exactly one tail chunk while earlier facts survive; \`--force\` re-dispatches every chunk; throttle window boundaries; branch+default sync ordering and default-only dedupe; empty-branch fallback; handler-level event gating (session_start does not sync/distill, checkpoint does, with the hinted session id).
- Full \`go test -race ./internal/cli\` passes (610s; note: the suite now sits right at go test's default 10m timeout on a laptop — CI's runners are faster).
- \`gofmt -s\`, \`go vet\` clean.

## Risk

Distill now runs per commit (throttled to once/60s) instead of per session end. Token spend is bounded by the chunk cache: each chunk of a session is distilled once in total, same as before — the spend moves earlier, it does not grow. A rewritten transcript history (condense/compaction) changes chunk hashes and honestly re-distills those chunks.

content.text:
Here's the full walk, from `git commit` to the plugin, with code references.

**When it gets called.** You commit → git runs the `post-commit` hook `entire enable` installed → `entire hooks git post-commit` → checkpoint capture → `ManualCommitStrategy.PostCommit` loops over the sessions with pending work. For each session whose condensation **actually produced this commit's checkpoint** (`condensed == true`, main's existing signal), it calls `brainnotify.Notify(worktreePath, EventCheckpoint, sessionID, branch)`. It does not fire when nothing condensed (a commit with no AI-session work), during rebase/cherry-pick sequence operations (PostCommit skips lifecycle transitions there — that's the second test), or from inside the Brain worker itself (`ENTIRE_BRAIN_MEMORY_WORKER=1` guard, loop prevention).

**How it gets called / sent.** There is no IPC, socket, queue, or file protocol. `Notify` builds the argv `brain memory notify --event checkpoint --session <id> --branch <b>` — content-free routing metadata, never transcript content — and hands it to `execx.SpawnDetached`, which **re-execs the `entire` binary itself** (`os.Executable()`) as a detached child: new session on Unix, detached process group on Windows, stdout/stderr discarded, cwd set to the repo root, process released so it outlives the hook. Inside that child, the host's normal plugin dispatcher resolves the `brain` verb to the managed entire-brain binary and execs it. So the "event bus" is: spawn one short-lived process that is just another `entire brain …` invocation.

**Failure modes, and what each costs:**

| Failure | Behavior | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| `os.Executable()` or `Start()` fails | swallowed, hook unaffected | one missed hint |
| Plugin not installed | child's dispatcher errors; detached child has no TTY, so no install prompt; output discarded | one short-lived no-op process per commit |
| Repo not brain-enabled / brain paused | plugin exits silently (`backgroundPaused`, repo resolution guards) | nothing |
| Plugin crashes mid-work | detached, output discarded | missed hint |
| Condense succeeded but state save failed | hint still fires (it's advisory); worker finds nothing new | one wasted nudge |
| Commit burst (rebase with many commits, many sessions in one commit) | one spawn per condensed session, but the plugin's claim-first 60s throttle collapses them; losers exit in milliseconds | a few empty processes |
| Hint lost for any reason above | the daemon tick and reconciliation pass pick the work up later | staleness only — **a lost hint can never lose data or misplace a fact**, which is the design's one load-bearing property |

**Is there a simpler way?** I looked at the alternatives honestly:

- *Plugin installs its own post-commit git hook*: git allows one hook per name, entire already owns it, chaining is brittle — and the plugin wouldn't know **which session** condensed into the checkpoint. That session↔checkpoint mapping is information only the host has at that moment, and it's the payload that makes the hint useful.
- *Synchronous call inside the hook*: violates the never-block-the-commit rule.
- *Host writes a hint file, plugin daemon picks it up*: avoids the spawn, but only works when a resident daemon is running — and it often isn't. The spawn is what makes this work daemon-free: the notify child itself launches the worker on demand.
- *Do nothing, rely on the daemon tick*: that's the status quo this fixes.

So the spawn is already the minimal mechanism satisfying the four constraints (never block the commit, no resident daemon required, carries the session id, no new protocol). The one marginal simplification available: stat the plugins dir before spawning so a machine without the plugin doesn't pay one empty process per commit — I left it out as a micro-optimization, but it's a two-line add if the empty spawn bothers you.

**If brain is not installed:** `Notify` still spawns (the host deliberately doesn't know about plugin inventory), the child's plugin dispatcher fails to resolve `brain`, the error would normally prompt "install the plugin?" but a detached child can't prompt, so it prints the non-interactive error into the discarded stderr and exits. The commit, the hook, and the user see nothing. Cost: ~one process spawn per condensed session per commit, a few milliseconds. If that's unacceptable, the stat-before-spawn check above removes it.

# Review PR

Review a pull request with structured, actionable feedback.

## Arguments

- `this PR. especially for simplicitiy` — PR number, URL, or branch name. If empty, review the current branch's open PR.

## Process

### 1. Fetch PR context

```
gh pr view <pr> --json title,body,baseRefName,headRefName,additions,deletions,changedFiles,commits,author
gh pr diff <pr>
```

Read the PR description carefully — it defines scope and intent. Everything you review should be evaluated against what the PR is trying to accomplish.

### 2. Understand the change

Before reviewing line-by-line:
- What is this PR doing and why?
- What files are touched and what's the blast radius?
- Are there any architectural implications?

### 3. Review with this checklist

**Correctness**
- Does the code do what the PR description says?
- Are there logic errors, off-by-one bugs, or unhandled edge cases?
- Are error paths handled correctly?

**Security**
- Any injection risks (SQL, XSS, command injection)?
- Are secrets, tokens, or credentials handled safely?
- Are inputs validated at system boundaries?

**Testing**
- Are there tests for the new/changed behavior?
- Do tests cover edge cases, not just the happy path?
- Are test assertions meaningful (not just "doesn't throw")?

**Design**
- Does the change follow existing codebase patterns and conventions?
- Is the abstraction level appropriate (not over/under-engineered)?
- Are there unnecessary changes outside the stated scope?

**Performance**
- Any N+1 queries, unbounded loops, or missing pagination?
- Are there opportunities for batching or caching that were missed?
- Will this scale with the data sizes it will encounter?

**Readability**
- Are names clear and consistent with the codebase?
- Is complex logic adequately explained?
- Would a future reader understand the "why" behind non-obvious decisions?

### 4. Adversarial review

Take a second, adversarial pass over the diff. Actively try to break the change — assume it has flaws and hunt for them across:

- **Performance** — worst-case inputs, hot paths, allocations, contention.
- **Stability** — race conditions, partial failures, retries, resource leaks, crash recovery.
- **Correctness** — inputs and states that violate the author's assumptions.
- **Simplicity** — code that could be deleted or replaced with something simpler/stdlib.
- **Platform design standards** — deviations from the platform's established design patterns and conventions.

Add any findings to the output using the same severity format.

### 5. Run /simplify

Run the `/simplify` skill (via the Skill tool) against the changed code and fold its findings into the review output.

### 6. Structure your output

For each finding, use this format:

**[severity] file:line — short title**
Description of the issue and why it matters. Include a suggested fix when possible.

Severity levels:
- **[blocking]** — Must fix before merge. Correctness bugs, security issues, data loss risks.
- **[important]** — Should fix. Design problems, missing tests for critical paths, performance issues.
- **[nit]** — Nice to fix. Style, naming, minor improvements. Don't block merge on these.
- **[question]** — Not necessarily wrong, but needs clarification or discussion.

### 7. Summary

End with a brief summary:
- Overall assessment (approve / request changes / needs discussion)
- What the PR does well
- Top 1-3 items that need attention
- Any scope concerns (changes that seem unrelated to the stated goal)

## Guidelines

- Review what's in the diff, not what you wish was there. Don't request unrelated refactoring.
- If the PR is large, focus on the most impactful files first.
- Be specific — "this could be better" is not useful. Show what "better" looks like.
- Distinguish between "this is wrong" and "I would do this differently." Only the former is blocking.
- If you're unsure about something, use [question] severity instead of asserting it's wrong.
- Read relevant source files (not just the diff) when you need context about how changed code integrates with the rest of the system.

+// Package brainnotify sends content-free lifecycle hints to the optional
+// Entire Brain plugin without putting plugin work on a host hook's critical
+// path.
+package brainnotify
+
+import (
+	"os"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/execx"
+)
+
+// Event is a lifecycle event understood by `entire brain memory notify`.
+type Event string
+
+const (
+	EventSessionStart Event = "session_start"
+	EventCheckpoint   Event = "checkpoint"
+	EventSessionEnd   Event = "session_end"
+
+	memoryWorkerOriginEnv = "ENTIRE_BRAIN_MEMORY_WORKER"
+)
+
+var spawnDetached = execx.SpawnDetached
+
+// Notify launches `entire brain memory notify` as detached, best-effort work.
+// The argv is deliberately limited to content-free routing metadata. Repository
+// identity stays owned by Brain, which resolves it from repoRoot.
+//
+// Notify has no result by design: a missing or failing Brain plugin must never
+// change the host hook's result or output. Canonical reconciliation repairs a
+// missed hint later.
+func Notify(repoRoot string, event Event, sessionID, branch string) {
+	if os.Getenv(memoryWorkerOriginEnv) == "1" {
+		return
+	}
+	if strings.TrimSpace(repoRoot) == "" || strings.TrimSpace(sessionID) == "" || !event.valid() {
+		return
+	}
+
+	args := []string{
+		"brain", "memory", "notify",
+		"--event", string(event),
+		"--session", sessionID,
+	}
+	if branch != "" {
+		args = append(args, "--branch", branch)
+	}
+
+	spawnDetached(repoRoot, args...)
+}
+
+func (e Event) valid() bool {
+	switch e {
+	case EventSessionStart, EventCheckpoint, EventSessionEnd:
+		return true
+	default:
+		return false
+	}
+}

`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

## Review: entireio/cli#2784 — simplicity focus

**[important] strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go — hint bypassed the save gate — FIXED**
The hint fired in the loop body after `MutateSessionStateOnSaved` returned, so it fired even when the save failed or skipped. That mechanism's doc (session_state.go:560) explicitly names "detached process spawn" as an intended `onSaved` effect, and `condensedTelemetry.emit` right next to it honors the discipline. Moved the hint into the `onSaved` callback — simpler *and* more correct. (Altitude agent; I had wrongly rationalized this as "advisory, harmless" in the original PR.)

**[important] strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:70 — seam var orphaned a doc comment — FIXED**
My insertion landed between `errPromptTimedOut`'s doc comment and its declaration. Three of four agents flagged it independently. Moved.

**[nit] brainnotify — dead event surface — FIXED**
`EventSessionStart`, `EventSessionEnd`, the `Event` type, and the `valid()` switch had zero production callers (session-end is deprecated as a trigger; the compiler already prevents the mistake `valid()` guarded). Collapsed to one function, `NotifyCheckpoint(repoRoot, sessionID, branch)` — the package is now ~55 lines, and the events return with their call sites if ever.

**[nit] brainnotify — fork per commit on plugin-less machines — FIXED**
Brain is optional, so "not installed" is the common case, and each condensed session cost a full `entire` re-exec that only discovered the plugin is missing. Added a `LookPath("entire-brain")` guard (verified: main.go prepends the managed plugin dir to PATH, so this resolves managed installs) — a stat instead of a fork.

**[nit] strategy — `GetCurrentBranchName(repo)` per loop iteration — FIXED**
One `.git/HEAD` read + ref resolution per session for a value that can't change mid-PostCommit. Hoisted above the loop.

**[question] one spawn per condensed session — SKIPPED, deliberate**
Batching into one spawn per commit needs a repeatable `--session` flag on the plugin side (cross-repo contract change), the plugin's 60s claim-first throttle already collapses the burst, and multi-session commits are rare. Not worth the contract churn now.

**[nit] worker-origin env var owned by the other repo — ADDRESSED via comment**
The plugin's own notify handler is the real recursion guard (verified in `memory_cmd.go`); the host-side check is now documented as a spawn-cost optimization, so a plugin-side rename can't silently remove protection.

**Clean:** reuse (correctly uses `execx.SpawnDetached` and matches the repo's seam-var conventions — `sweepSpawn`, `trailRefreshSpawn`), mechanism altitude (no generic host→plugin event bus exists to reuse; `PostCommit` is the right layer since both condense paths converge there and only the host knows session+branch at that moment).

**Summary: approve, with the five fixes now in the PR.** The PR does the core thing right — detached, never-fails, content-free, reuses existing machinery — and the review made it ~90 lines lighter and save-gated. Known accepted gap, stated in the PR body: the condense-*failure* no-hint path is covered only indirectly (its old test's injection helper no longer exists; the `onSaved` move actually strengthens this — a failed save now structurally can't hint).
